$comment: U59 -- the three board defects an eight-lens adversarial review found in the
work of U51..U58. All three were introduced by that work; none was caught by
DRC, and two of them cannot be.
1. TP2's SOLDER MASK MERGES WITH C34's PAD. This is the real one.
U53 untented three vias as rail probe points. Two are fine. The third, TP2 on
/+3V3 at (135.508,110.254), sits 0.0295 mm from C34 pad 1 -- against the
board's own 0.100 mm minimum mask width. The dam cannot be plotted and cannot
be printed: in the exported F_Mask.gbr, TP1 and TP3 each get a discrete
0.5949 mm circular opening and TP2 gets NO opening at all, only a merged
1.4084 x 1.3064 mm blob spanning the via and the pad together. KiCad removed
the sub-minimum web itself.
So at reflow C34's pad-1 paste has an open 0.25 mm barrel 0.33 mm away to
drain into, while pad 2 (/GND, thermal to the pour) wets normally -- starved
or open joint, or a tombstoned 0603, on an MCU rail decoupler. The field
symptom is intermittent, not dead.
DRC CANNOT SEE THIS AND REPORTS 0/0/0 TRUTHFULLY. solder_mask_bridge only
fires between apertures of DIFFERENT nets, and the via and the pad are both
/+3V3. Baseline origin/main had zero mask dams below 0.15 mm; U53 created it.
Fix: re-tent TP2, untent the /+3V3 via at (121.314,99.332) instead. That is
the ONLY /+3V3 via on the board clean on both counts -- 1.3174 mm mask dam,
1.038 mm clear of any courtyard. Two candidates that look better on mask dam
courtyards respectively; that only shows up if the courtyard is tested as a
POLYGON rather than a bounding box, which is how one reviewer got it wrong.
It moves TP2 from 5.07 mm to 14.4 mm from TP3. That costs nothing: TP2 exists
for a DMM rail check, not a scope ground.
U53's own note claimed 'none of them under a component courtyard'. TP2's
copper laps 0.234 mm inside C34's. That claim was made by testing the via
CENTRE instead of its shape -- the exact error CLAUDE.md's window-query rule
exists to prevent, made in the unit that cites it.
2. C46 IS 502.6 nm FROM A /GND TRACK -- the tightest thing U51..U58 created.
U52 moved C46 to (132.000,113.048). Its pad 1 (/NRST) ends up 0.102103 mm
from the /GND diagonal (130.442,111.016)->(135.014,115.588), against a
0.1016 mm rule. Legal by 502.6 nm, and second-tightest on the whole board
after a pre-existing pair at 71.6 nm.
It is worth the edit because of WHICH net it is. /NRST shorted to /GND holds
the H7 in permanent reset: the board powers up, both new rail probes read
good, and nothing renders, with no error and no distinguishing symptom. That
is precisely the diagnostic hole U52's own rationale argues against.
C46 moves 0.15 mm along the perpendicular to that diagonal -- the minimum
disturbance that buys real margin, 0.1021 -> 0.2521 mm. The /NRST stub is
re-laid to the new pad centre; its far end at the existing escape via
(130.442,113.048) does not move, so nothing upstream changes.
Worth recording why it was missed: U52's clearance work went entirely into
the VIA question, where it correctly caught a hole_to_hole trap at 0.258 mm
against a same-net via. It never measured the pad it was about to land.
3. FOUR REFERENCE DESIGNATORS APPEARED ON THE SILKSCREEN.
JLCImport:ERJP06F60R4V ships its Reference field VISIBLE; the R0603 instances
it replaced had it hidden. So U57 left R10/R14/R15/R24 as the only 4 of 150
footprints with a printed designator, on a board whose convention is to
silkscreen function (BTN1-4, BOOT, RESET, CAN1/2, TT1-8, H/L) and never
designators. F.Fab is not in kicad_fab.py's exported layer set, so this is
what the assembly house actually receives.
Hidden again here, restoring the convention. Note this is the same lesson U57
already banked -- 'swapping a land pattern re-seats the reference designator'
-- one step further: it can also un-hide it.
NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately, and recorded in the triage instead: the lib_id
of R10/R14/R15/R24 and C41/C42 still points at the pre-swap symbol, so a GUI
'Update Symbols from Library' would silently revert their supplier fields
while the board keeps the new land patterns. --schematic-parity catches the
footprint half and nothing catches the supplier half. Fixing it is a GUI
Change Symbol on ten designators; it is schematic-only, with no footprint,
net or routing consequence.

steps.step: 1/3  move the /+3V3 probe point off C34's pad
2/3  back C46 away from the /GND diagonal, and re-land its stub
3/3  hide the four designators the 0805 land pattern un-hid
